claims.head: Strength against strength
claims.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, and the Avalanche are one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Penguins.
claims.call: The Penguins’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Avalanche.
claims.nums: Pittsburgh 3rd for chance quality (a 6.9% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Colorado 2nd for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: It’s strength against strength: the Penguins for chance quality, the Avalanche at preventing dangerous shots.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 5 and 4 games this season

check.measure: the average shot’s chance of going in, by expected goals
check.rule: held if tonight's figure lands on the predicted side of the league average; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Expect the Avalanche to fire from everywhere
claims.call: The Avalanche take at least their usual 70.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: Few teams shoot like the Avalanche, and the Penguins are near the bottom of the league at keeping shots away. It could be a long night in the Penguins’ end.
claims.nums: Colorado 1st for shot volume (70.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Pittsburgh 23rd for shot suppression
claims.gist: The Avalanche shoot a lot, and the Penguins give up plenty.

check.measure: 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, adjusted for score and venue
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Shots should fly both ways
claims.call: The game runs at more than 89.0 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
claims.body: Pittsburgh plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Colorado. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
claims.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Pittsburgh 3rd (84.9), Colorado 1st (89.0)
claims.gist: Both teams like a fast game.

check.rule: held if tonight's pace is above the faster team's usual; partly if above the league average; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: In close against from distance
claims.body: The Penguins are the league’s best for shots from in close, at the close-range end; the Avalanche are one of the league’s worst, at the long-range end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.nums: Shots from in close: Pittsburgh 1st, Colorado 31st
claims.gist: The Penguins and the Avalanche sit at opposite ends for shots from in close.
claims.call: The Penguins take a bigger share of their shots from within 20 feet than the Avalanche.

COL.head: Colorado should have the upper hand
COL.body: Colorado has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Pittsburgh’s way back in is a penalty kill that holds up.

PIT.head: Pittsburgh faces a real test
PIT.body: Colorado has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Pittsburgh can pull it off if their penalty kill holds up.

story.head: Strength against strength
paras: The Avalanche are 3-1-0. The Penguins haven’t won in three.
It’s strength against strength: the Penguins for chance quality, the Avalanche at preventing dangerous shots. The Avalanche shoot a lot, and the Penguins give up plenty.

lean.COL: Colorado has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Pittsburgh’s way back in is a penalty kill that holds up.

items.text: Bryan Rust has a point in six straight games against Colorado.
Nathan MacKinnon has a point in five straight games against Pittsburgh, and 12 points in his last six against them.
Samuel Girard faces his old team, Colorado.
Sidney Crosby is still looking for his first goal of the season.
